skills.name: product-engineering-essentials
skills.title: Product Engineering Essentials
skills.summary: Checks how much foundational product-engineering groundwork the repository actually has in place, across ten pillars: product vision & problem definition, user & domain understanding, product requirements & scope, UX/product design foundation, architecture & technical foundation, development standards & engineering practices, DevOps & environment foundation, quality engineering foundation, security/compliance & operational readiness, and the product delivery & feedback loop. Reads the real repository — docs, CI config, infra, test structure, whatever exists — and marks each item In place / Partial / Missing / N/A with evidence, never inferring a status from a file's mere existence. Produces a checklist report, not a score, since the pillars are not equally weighted or equally urgent for every project. Not a gate — nothing blocks on it; it exists purely to make gaps visible so a team chooses deliberately rather than by accident.
skills.whenToInvoke: any time the team wants a shared, evidence-based picture of what foundational product/engineering artifacts exist and which are missing — often useful early, but equally useful mid-project as a sanity check before scaling up
skills.howToInvoke: Read process-onboarding-agent/skills/product-engineering-essentials.md and run the essentials check on this repository.

skills.name: solution-shaping
skills.title: Solution Shaping
skills.summary: Decides the shape of a solution before any design work begins: generic capability or feature-specific implementation, expected usage and scale, the simplest viable approach, extend-vs-build-vs-buy, and how reversible the choice is. The signed-off decision is recorded on the feature brief and constrains the design session that follows — so over-engineering and accidental platform-building are caught before any contract is drawn.
skills.whenToInvoke: when a high-level feature request lands, before running a design session or breaking work into tasks
skills.howToInvoke: Read process-onboarding-agent/skills/solution-shaping.md and shape the solution for [feature name].

skills.name: design-session
skills.title: Design Session
skills.summary: Runs a structured Phase 0 design session before any building begins. Locks down API contracts, data model decisions, and architectural patterns through conversation, then produces a design artifact the team can reference during build.
skills.whenToInvoke: at the start of planning a new feature, before breaking it into tasks
skills.howToInvoke: Read process-onboarding-agent/skills/design-session.md and run a design session for [feature name].

skills.name: bolt-risk-assessment
skills.title: Risk Assessment
skills.summary: Runs a structured risk assessment before a batch of work executes. Interrogates blast radius, cross-component risks, rollback options, and whether a feature flag is warranted.
skills.whenToInvoke: before starting a sizeable feature, refactor, or infrastructure change
skills.howToInvoke: Read process-onboarding-agent/skills/bolt-risk-assessment.md and run a risk assessment for [work description].

skills.name: uat
skills.title: UAT Sign-off
skills.summary: Generates a plain-language UAT demo script from a set of acceptance criteria, walks the engineer through each step, and records pass/fail/deferred outcomes. Blocks closure of a feature until a sign-off status is recorded.
skills.whenToInvoke: when a feature is complete and ready for acceptance testing with the stakeholder or product owner
skills.howToInvoke: Read process-onboarding-agent/skills/uat.md and run a UAT session for [feature name] using these acceptance criteria: [paste ACs].

skills.name: release-readiness-checklist
skills.title: Release Readiness Checklist
skills.summary: Walks the engineer through the UAT Release Checklist or the Production Release Checklist, one item at a time, before a release ships. Records Confirmed / Not confirmed / N/A for every item, captures a blocker note for anything not confirmed, and closes with a full readiness report. Not an evidence audit — unlike Product Engineering Essentials, it never inspects the repository, CI logs, or any other artifact; it is a pure self-attestation record. It never gates or authorizes the release either — that decision stays with whoever holds sign-off (technical owner, QA, security, product, operations, as applicable).
skills.whenToInvoke: before deploying a build to a UAT environment, and again before a production release
skills.howToInvoke: Read process-onboarding-agent/skills/release-readiness-checklist.md and run the [UAT|Production] release checklist for [version/build].

skills.name: root-cause-analysis
skills.title: Root Cause Analysis
skills.summary: Applies structured 5-Whys analysis to a resolved incident or recurring problem. Classifies the root cause as Solution Design, Technology Selection, or Process, and proposes concrete remediation actions.
skills.whenToInvoke: after a production incident is resolved, or when a pattern of recurring bugs is noticed
skills.howToInvoke: Read process-onboarding-agent/skills/root-cause-analysis.md and run a root cause analysis on [incident description].

skills.name: hotfix-bolt
skills.title: Hotfix Workflow
skills.summary: Runs an emergency intake for a production incident: three questions (symptom, severity, rollback availability), a minimal unit of work, blast radius check, and a mandatory retro within 24 hours.
skills.whenToInvoke: when a production incident needs an immediate response
skills.howToInvoke: Read process-onboarding-agent/skills/hotfix-bolt.md and start a hotfix for [symptom].

skills.name: process-visualization
skills.title: Process Visualization
skills.summary: Reconstructs how a batch of work actually got delivered — not the plan, but what really happened — and renders it as Mermaid diagrams: an actual delivery timeline and an actual execution path, plus a plan-vs-actual deviation table. Mines git history for real status-change dates when the project is a git repo; falls back to whatever dates are recorded in your own artifacts otherwise, and says plainly which mode it used.
skills.whenToInvoke: at the start of a retrospective, before discussing what went well — or any time you want a factual reconstruction of how a piece of work actually unfolded
skills.howToInvoke: Read process-onboarding-agent/skills/process-visualization.md and visualize how [bolt/feature name] actually went.

skills.name: progress-digest
skills.title: Progress Digest
skills.summary: Generates a plain-language, one-page progress summary for a feature — written for non-technical stakeholders. Translates the current state of a feature into what is being built, what is done, and what comes next.
skills.whenToInvoke: when a stakeholder update is needed, or before a sprint review
skills.howToInvoke: Read process-onboarding-agent/skills/progress-digest.md and generate a progress digest for [feature name]. Here is the current state: [describe or paste context].

skills.name: knowledge-promotion
skills.title: Knowledge Promotion
skills.summary: Evaluates improvements or learnings from a retro or incident and classifies each as generic (shareable across teams) or project-specific (keep local). For generic improvements, drafts the exact change needed in shared resources so the engineer can raise it with the wider team or guild.
skills.whenToInvoke: at the end of a retrospective, after applying improvements
skills.howToInvoke: Read process-onboarding-agent/skills/knowledge-promotion.md and run knowledge promotion on these retro improvements: [paste improvements].

skills.name: notifications
skills.title: Notifications
skills.summary: Sends Slack alerts at the delivery moments that need a human — sign-off required, work complete, incident, repeated failure. A local, per-engineer setup: your own channel, your own webhook, your own machine, notifying you about your own sessions — not a team broadcast. Two layers: deterministic tool hooks that ping every time the agent stops or needs attention — supported on Claude Code, Cursor and Copilot, each with its own config file — and agent-driven, event-specific notifications you can wire into any process.
skills.whenToInvoke: when you want to be pinged instead of watching a session — e.g. long-running work, async review, or on-call

skills.name: ai-hub-metrics
skills.title: AI Hub Metrics
skills.summary: Pushes usage and activity events to 99x AI Hub at delivery moments that mark real progress — attributing each event to the actors who did the work (human, AI, or both) and, when tracked separately, tokens/cost/model. This is a project-wide integration (one Team, one Workflow, one shared credential in AI Hub), not a per-engineer setup like notifications.
skills.whenToInvoke: when the team wants AI-assisted delivery work visible in a shared usage dashboard — tokens, cost, model, and who participated, across the team
skills.howToInvoke: Read process-onboarding-agent/skills/ai-hub-metrics.md and push an AI Hub event for [unit/bolt/intent].

skills.name: dependency-audit
skills.title: Dependency Audit
skills.summary: Reads package manifests, classifies findings by severity (critical / high / medium / low), and produces a remediation list with suggested actions for high and critical issues.
skills.whenToInvoke: monthly, or before a release, or whenever a security advisory is published for a dependency you use
skills.howToInvoke: Read process-onboarding-agent/skills/dependency-audit.md and run a dependency audit on this project.

skills.name: compact-docs
skills.title: Compact Docs
skills.summary: Archives operational documents older than a configured threshold — keeping the active workspace clean without losing institutional memory.
skills.whenToInvoke: when your process documents folder has grown large and is hard to navigate, or at a cadence your team sets (e.g., end of each sprint)
skills.howToInvoke: Read process-onboarding-agent/skills/compact-docs.md and archive documents older than [N] days in [folder path].

skills.name: process-health
skills.title: Process Health
skills.summary: Computes four process health metrics — improvement adoption rate, quality gate failure rate, AC revision rate, and bolt velocity — and surfaces decay signals. Saves a dated health report automatically.
skills.whenToInvoke: periodically (e.g., every few sprints) to check whether process discipline is holding or drifting
skills.howToInvoke: Read process-onboarding-agent/skills/process-health.md and run a process health check. The project is [project name] and our process artifacts are at [folder path].

skills.name: new-engineer-induction
skills.title: New Engineer Induction
skills.summary: Walks a new team member through the project's governance framework, explains each section in plain language, demonstrates the quality gate with a project-specific example, and produces a personalized quick-reference card.

skills.name: governance-map
skills.title: Governance Map
skills.summary: Draws a one-page map of how the installed framework governs delivery — the governance layer, each phase's steps, every sign-off gate, the bolt variants and the feedback loops — built only from the project's own framework files, as a Mermaid Markdown file and a self-contained HTML blueprint.

skills.name: bug-bolt
skills.title: Bug Bolt
skills.summary: Lightweight workflow for fixing a specific, reproducible bug — four-question intake, recurrence check, single focused unit, mandatory RCA if recurring.

skills.name: nfr-bolt
skills.title: NFR Bolt
skills.summary: Non-functional improvement workflow — measurable threshold AC, before/after baseline, cross-reference to affected features.

agents.name: Onboarding
agents.does: Installs the 99x Intent Delivery Framework through a structured interview or codebase archaeology session

agents.name: Experience
agents.does: Governs AI behavior on every working session — quality gates, elaboration, bolts, retros, UAT
agents.entryPoint: Master rule file (auto-loaded at session start)

agents.name: Diagnostics
agents.does: Audits process against AI-DLC principles and delivers a structured gap report — works with or without the framework installed

agents.name: Skills
agents.does: Installs individual framework skills into a bespoke delivery process without installing the full framework

agents.name: Migration
agents.does: Migrates a project from the old ai-dlc/ structure to the new methodology

agents.name: Estimation
agents.does: Produces structured estimates — ballpark ranges from draft requirements (pre-sales/feasibility) or bolt-level delivery estimates from elaborated units (release planning)

phases.title: Easy wins: add AI to what you already do
phases.intro: No process change required. These activities slot into existing ceremonies and produce immediate, visible output.

activities.does: Turns a planning or discovery transcript into draft stories, tasks, and open questions.
Rewrites a rough story in intent style — what it is, why it matters, and what success looks like.
Expands a story into testable acceptance criteria plus non-functional requirements: performance, security, accessibility, and observability.
Turns ticket moves and commits into a plain-language stakeholder update.
Writes the "what changed and why" on each pull request so reviewers start faster and with full context.

phases.title: Strengthen the ceremony: AI adds judgment, not just text
phases.intro: These activities deepen the quality of decisions your team already makes. The AI does not just produce text — it challenges assumptions and surfaces risk.

activities.does: Before story sign-off, asks "what could break or go unhandled?" on each story.
Checks diffs for security gaps, missing error handling, and test coverage before merge.
Drafts test cases and a UAT demo script directly from the acceptance criteria.
Takes retro notes, clusters themes by type, ranks them, and proposes concrete actions with suggested owners.
Runs root-cause analysis on a production incident and classifies the cause as design / technology / process.
Flags vague, duplicate, or oversized tickets and suggests how to split or sharpen them.

phases.title: Approaching AI-DLC discipline: the loop starts to close
phases.intro: By this phase, the team is running a recognizable version of the AI-DLC cycle. Completing items 12–17 is the practical signal that formal onboarding will land on fertile ground rather than on an unfamiliar process.

activities.does: Drafts the actual rule or checklist update so a retro finding becomes an applied change within the same sprint.
Helps the team lock API contracts, data models, and architectural constraints before any building begins.
Before a sizeable change, assesses impact on other components, rollback options, and whether a feature flag is needed.
Reads package manifests monthly, lists risky or outdated packages, and suggests remediation steps.
Walks a new engineer through the codebase and produces a personalized quick-reference card.
Seeds a CLAUDE.md or .cursor/rules/project-rules.mdc with the team's actual coding standards and domain terms — the first step of a real onboarding.
activities.buildsToward: Master rule file → full framework adoption
